Home / About us / Headteacher’s letter
There is a vibrancy at Torriano Primary School which has an impact on all who visit. The school’s distinct atmosphere is a result of the combination of high aspirations, innovation and a relentless focus on excellence in all areas of the school.
Through our commitment to the Rights of the Child, we are passionate about young people’s learning and relish the challenge of guiding our children through the early stages of their lives. Torriano is an outstanding two-form entry primary school in Kentish Town, Camden. The culture of our school ensures that every child is known well and valued. We are a happy, ambitious and inclusive school reflecting the rich diversity of families in our area. It is a safe and stimulating environment for learning, playing and growing.
Torriano is a rights respecting community, which promotes active, global citizenship. We have an energetic and enthusiastic pupil voice, developed by a strong oracy curriculum. This champions the rights of learners and strives to provide a purposeful and learning climate. We believe that communication underpins cooperation and collaboration. Both must be taught and practised explicitly, in appropriate ways for all learners. Education builds the capacities of individuals to work together, to collaborate, to transform themselves, their communities, and the wider world.
Torriano is rooted in the heart of our community. We value strong relationships and partnerships, both with our families and also local and national organisations that enrich our curriculum. We are federated with Brecknock Primary School through Executive Headship and have established a strong commitment to excellence and equity in our local area. We share a growing professional learning community across the partnership, developing pedagogy, curriculum and innovation for everyone, through training, research and evidence informed practice. We have developed a team of expert and specialist teachers and leaders, who support and grow other professionals at a local and national level.
We specialise in science teaching, as a Primary Science Quality Mark Outreach school, our teachers have expert training. We have a state of the art, award winning Science Lab and Scientist in Residence from The Crick Institute, which helps to develop strong science capital for all at Torriano. We have a long standing commitment to primary careers education through our commitment to STEAM partnerships.
At Torriano we place a strong emphasis on creativity with a spotlight on performing and visual arts – including art, music, drama and dance. We offer an enriched curriculum where the children’s heritage is valued and celebrated.
At Torriano we are happy, have mutual respect and work hard. The physical and mental well being of all our children is equally valued, with prominence in the curriculum. We have a dedicated pastoral care team that ensures every child gets the support they need. Torriano has an expansive PE provision, which champions inclusive practice and leads to sporting success locally and regionally.
We are very proud of our children and the team who help them learn. We encourage any prospective families to visit us and experience the Torriano community first hand. We look forward to meeting you!
Helen Bruckdorfer and Holly Churchill
Executive Headteacher and Head of School

Home / Wellbeing School / UNICEF Rights Respecting School
UNICEF Rights Respecting School
Torriano Primary School is a Gold Rights Respecting School, and this key principle underpins the whole school policy for promoting positive behaviour. A Rights Respecting School since 2009, we have advocated for global equality and campaigned on local and global issues, ensuring our children see themselves as part of a global family.
The United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC) is the cornerstone of our whole school policy for promoting positive behaviour. The Convention is the most widely-ratified international human rights treaty in history. It has 54 articles that cover all aspects of a child’s life and set out the civil, political, economic, social and cultural rights that all children everywhere are entitled to. These rights describe what a child needs to survive, grow, and live up to their potential individual liberty. They apply equally to every child, no matter who they are or where they come from.
In teaching and learning, both in the classroom and in assemblies, children consider how some children are unable to access their rights, linking carefully to the Sustainable Development Goals. Through this lens, we also teach them about the five British values:
Democracy
The rule of law
Individual liberty
Mutual respect

Home / About us / Brecknock & Torriano Schools Federation
The Brecknock and Torriano Federation was formed in 2022. We share a governing board, and an Executive Headteacher with strategic responsibility for both schools.
By working together, our schools are able to share expertise, resources and create greater opportunities and capacity, whilst at the same time allowing each school to flourish with its own identity and community.
Aligned in our vision and goals, we believe that education builds the capacities of individuals to work together, to collaborate, to transform themselves, their communities, and the wider world.
We strive to provide a high-quality education and promote success for all pupils. Our collective mission is for all children to have a future of choice and opportunity.
Through collaboration, we provide great teaching, strong leadership and a federation curriculum that aims for children to be knowledgable learners, confident communicators and active local and global citizens.
Our children have opportunities to learn, play and grow together, united in collective action for our communities.

Home / Extra-curricular / Extended Hours
Extended Hours
Children in the Early Years (Nursery and Reception) are able to access our Extended Hours provision. This provision, available only to our youngest children, enables the children to stay at school until up to 6pm every day. The Extended Hours service takes place in the EYFS environment, where the children play, have a snack provided, take part in activities and relax.
Children can attend for as many days as needed in the week, however we require a half term’s notice for any changes. Please note that the children do not receive a hot meal.

£14 per day until 6pm
There is a late charge of £6 if you do not pick your child up by 6pm.

Home / Extra-curricular / Residential trips
Residential trips
Residentials are an integral part of the educational offer for all children at Torriano and Brecknock. We value the importance of increasing their connectivity with nature, embedding climate and nature into their learning in real life contexts. This not only supports our science and geography curriculum, it also supports the development of children’s physical health and mental well-being.
Year 6 – PARIS
The culmination of children’s French language and geography learning, Year 6 visit Paris for a four day residential trip. Taking place in the summer term, the children visit a local market to practise their language skills, enjoy the rides of Parc Asterix and explore the sights of Paris via the River Seine and a walk up to Montmartre. They compare the physical and human geography of areas of Paris and London. It is a once in a lifetime trip where the children are immersed in French and one they never forget!
Year 5 – BURWELL HOUSE
Year 5 children have the opportunity to visit Burwell House, in the Cambridgeshire countryside, for two nights. This residential trip has a geography and outdoor learning focus as part of a high-quality geography education which aims to inspire in pupils a curiosity and fascination about the world and its people that will remain with them for the rest of their lives. Orienteering through The Fens, exploring the local woodland and seeing first hand a range of diverse natural environments, the children’s geography learning comes to life.
Year 4 – DEBDEN HOUSE
Children in Year 4 spend a summer night camping at Debden House in Epping Forest. Building dens, roasting marshmallows, whittling sticks and navigating the woodland, children make memories in the great outdoors, learning how to be more independent. They hone their Ordnance Survey map skills and consider the different uses of the forest by humans over time.

Home / Inclusion / SEND Information Report
Our Director of Inclusion has overall responsibility for SEND and Inclusion. This means that we regularly discuss SEND issues in Senior Leadership Team meetings. We keep support for children with SEND under review.
Our Director of Inclusion manages our Inclusion Team. They oversee the day to day provision and programmes of support for individuals and small groups of pupils with SEND.
The inclusion team keeps an up to date record of children we identify as having a Special Educational Need or Disability.
The Director of Inclusion also keeps a record of the provision in place to support children with SEND, for example, support in reading, communication or maths.
A child’s provision is recorded within a My Plan document. This document is a record of short term targets, which we review termly.
We carefully monitor the progress and well-being of children with SEND and the quality of our provision, including teaching and support. For example, senior leaders observe lessons and small group work, as well as holding regular discussions with teachers and support staff.
If something is not working well, we change and improve our provision. We make sure that support is well-matched to a child’s needs. We also make sure that the provision is well researched and effective, firmly routed in evidence.
The Governing Body challenges us to make sure we constantly improve the quality of provision for children with SEND and the outcomes that they achieve.
We have several parents on the governing body and one of their roles is to represent the views and concerns of all parents, including those with children with SEND
We have an allocated SEND Governor. They meet with our inclusion team regularly and makes visits to classrooms, observing practice in learning and teaching.
We fully involve our governors when we review and revise our SEND policy and our SEND Information Report at the end of each school year.
Ofsted 2024 “Pupils with special educational needs and/or disabilities(SEND) are identified promptly. These pupils, including those that attend the resourcedprovision, are supported with effective adaptations. They receive the high-quality supportthat they need and are learning the curriculum well.”
All staff have regular training and guidance to meet the needs of our children. The Director of Inclusion works with the Senior Leadership Team to arrange and provide this training.
We have regular professional development each term where we make sure that staff;
We regularly undertake an audit of staff training needs, which includes knowledge and expertise about different areas of needs. We provide/arrange training for staff as a result of these audits. This may include training in Attention Autism, Lego Therapy, Makaton, Handwriting, OT support and Phonics. We provide further specialist training for staff who support children with the most complex needs.
We provide regular staff briefings on the procedures set out in our SEND policy and make this policy accessible for all staff.
We use the eight national Teaching Standards to develop the knowledge, skills and confidence of all of our teachers as part of their professional development. Our support staff team also have professional standards which are monitored throughout the year.
Torriano has a Language Resource Base, which is a specialist provision supporting children with DLD.
Staff work closely with relevant members of specialist services which provide support for our school. The services which are working in our school this year include:
We are also able to access support services from Islington Council for our children who are Islington residents.
These services provide a range of support including:
Each service has referral and eligibility criteria – this means that service support is targeted at children with higher levels of need. More information about these services can be found on Camden’s Local Offer website http://www.localoffer.camden.gov.uk/.
We will always involve families in any decisions about whether their child has a special educational need and the best ways to provide support. If your child requires these services we will involve you in the process at every stage. We will seek permission from you to make any referrals and explain these processes fully.
When a child starts at Torriano, we meet with families before they start school. We know that parents are the first educators of their child and we need their knowledge to plan effectively. We will also plan careful transitions for children starting at Torriano Primary School. Often our staff will speak with your child’s previous setting before your child joins our school.
We ask whether parents/carers have any concerns about their children, or if their child has any additional needs. This helps us to plan how we will support their child once they start school.
In addition, we assess all children in their first half term in our school through careful and sensitive classroom observation and an early review of progress. In Reception this takes place through the Reception Baseline Assessment (RBA). We also listen to children to find out how they are settling in to school. We continue to assess and monitor throughout the child’s time in school so that we can identify any special educational needs that might arise.
We take great care to establish whether lack of progress is because a pupil has English as an additional language (EAL), for example by talking to the child (and parents) in their home language.
We also work with specialist services, for example Educational Psychologists and Speech Therapists, where necessary. They can provide expertise in finding out the type and range of a child’s needs.
We follow Camden’s guidance for the identification of SEND.
We are committed to personalised planning and regular Assess Plan Do Review cycles to make sure that all children makes progress.
You can see more details on how we identify children with SEND in our SEND policy.
It is very important for our school that all of our children enjoy success and achievement, making good progress in learning.
We use the information we have about each child who has been identified as having SEND to plan a personal programme of SEND support. This is a child’s My Plan and will include termly outcomes (targets). It will be regularly reviewed and a copy will always be sent to families.
We develop this in partnership with parents and the child and will agree outcomes during our termly meetings with parents. A child’s My Plan will include short term outcomes (targets) and will describe how we will support a child to achieve their targets. We make sure that parents/carers know the next steps for learning for their child.
Once a term we review in school how well all children, including those with SEND, are progressing. We call this our Pupil Progress Meeting.
We will report formally once a year on the progress of all children, including those with SEND, through annual reports.
It is very important for our school that ALL of our children enjoy success and achievement and make good progress in learning.
We use the information we have about each child who has been identified as having SEND to plan a personal programme of SEND support. This is your child’s My Plan and will include termly outcomes (targets). It will be reviewed at least termly and a copy will always be sent to you.
We develop this in partnership with parents and the child and will agree outcomes during our termly structured conversation meetings with parents.
Your child’s My Plan will include short term outcomes (targets) and will describe how we will support your child to achieve these targets.
Once a term we review in school how well all children, including those with SEND, are progressing. We call this our Pupil Progress Meeting.
We will arrange a termly structured conversation meeting with parents of children with SEND to discuss how well they have progressed. We will agree new targets and sometimes think of different ways of supporting, for example, a small reading group with a trained member of staff or other interventions.
We make sure that parents/carers know the next steps for learning for their child.
We will report formally once a year on the progress of all children, including those with SEND and for some pupils we will provide more frequent reports.
We know that high quality teaching and well-matched support will make a big difference to the progress of children with SEND. The EEF guidance report on Special Educational Needs in Mainstream Schools says, “Pupils with Special Educational Needs and Disability (SEND) have the greatest need for excellent teaching and are entitled to provision that supports achievement at, and enjoyment of, school.”
Making sure that this happens in all classrooms is one of the most important things that our school leaders do. We make sure that all staff have a clear understanding of the learning needs of the children in their class.
Torriano leaders, including the Director of Inclusion, work closely with teachers and support staff to provide effective teaching and support for children with SEND in a variety of ways. These include:
We help all children to develop their skills as learners and to persevere when they find learning difficult.
We provide a curriculum that is broad, balanced, motivating and accessible to all children. We want our exciting curriculum to be one of the many reasons our children love coming to school!
We work hard to ensure that all of our children achieve in lots of different ways as well as academic learning – for example, in drama, sport, music, dance, showing leadership and taking on responsibilities.
We encourage children with SEND to play a full part in the life of our school. Many of our children with a special educational need have extra responsibilities. Taking such roles helps them to communicate more confidently with other children.
Our 2024 Ofsted report says, “Pupils…participate in a wide variety of competitive sports events all year round. Pupils do well in these competitions. Leaders actively ensurethat disadvantaged pupils and those with SEND can take part in these sporting events.”
We arrange a huge range of educational visits and make sure that all of our children can take part. We complete a risk assessment and, when necessary, make reasonable adjustments to plans and arrangements to make sure that all children can attend.
Children may access specialist interventions to accelerate their progress. We choose these interventions after looking carefully at research and evidence. These sessions run for a pre-determined time and are delivered by staff who have been trained accordingly.
Our Inclusion Team monitors the quality and effectiveness of these interventions. For example, we measure a reading level at the start of a reading intervention and then assess progress over time and levels of attainment. If a child is not making sufficient progress and/or is falling short of expectations, we will consider other forms of support in discussion with parents/carers and the child.

Additional staff provide support for learning in the classroom and in small groups.
We work hard to make sure that our school buildings and all classrooms are safe, stimulating and accessible.
We aim to make lessons varied, stimulating and highly visual to support children with a variety of learning needs. For example, each classroom must use a visual timetable before assembly every morning to map out the day ahead. Colourful semantics and Widgit symbols are included on displays, used in lesson presentations and resources.
We have an ongoing Accessibility Plan, through which we are making improvements to the school environment over time. For example, we aim to host many events in our downstairs hall or our lift-accessible Gatehouse to make sure that everyone can attend.
Specialist teams, for example physiotherapists or occupational therapists, provide guidance, advice and equipment for a child with particular access or support needs. We have a range of equipment designed to support the development of children’s coordination and motor skills. Children have access to adaptive resources e.g. wobble cushions, ear defenders, sand timers, adapted pencils. These can be requested from the inclusion team and are available for children in classrooms. For some children we provide technology including digital technology such as iPads and laptop computers.
We know that the active involvement of families in supporting the education of their child is one of the most important factors in ensuring a child’s success and achievement. We know that these adults are the first educators of their child and that we need their knowledge to plan effectively.
We will always involve families and children in planning and reviewing progress and have regular meetings scheduled with families to discuss their children’s progress.

We will also help and advise families on how to help their children make progress at home, for example in mathematics and reading.
We welcome and value feedback on how well we are working with our parents. We have a federation Stakeholder Forum which meets on a half-termly basis to share updates and gather feedback and ideas. We value the voice of our community and see this forum as hugely important. We also hold regular coffee mornings and parent workshops to support families.
We try to communicate in plain English and have several bi-lingual staff who can offer translation and interpretation services in Urdu, Somali, French, Arabic. With notice, we can arrange a translator in other languages.
